propositions: Two test-only reliability oracles consume 15–25 seconds of wall time per matrix cell due to production-scale real-time values (10s window, 15s loopback server, 1s per-attempt deadline, real 2s/4s retry sleeps) despite testing logical contracts about throughput, retry schedule, and process cleanup rather than elapsed time.

The slow-progress snapshot test must inject a 1-second low-speed window, sustain real loopback traffic above the configured floor for more than one complete window, and retain the assertion that sustained bytes are not classified as stall without changing production defaults.

The ACLI subprocess timeout test must inject sub-second call/grace/drain values, record the exact logical retry schedule [2, 4] without sleeping, launch exactly _MAX_ATTEMPTS real child sessions, and poll all spawned PIDs to confirm they are absent after terminal failure without changing production attempt count or cleanup logic.
Production timeout, stall, grace, drain, attempt, and backoff defaults must remain byte-unchanged and no production code paths may be modified.
Both test files must pass all tests and complete in low single-digit seconds without absolute upper-bound assertions, wall-clock thresholds, or runner changes.
